title: Payroll to General Ledger: The Reconciliation Most Books Skip
summary: Payroll general ledger reconciliation catches what a payroll sync hides. See the balances that must agree each month and what stale liabilities cost you.
body_markdown:
## What Payroll General Ledger Reconciliation Is


Payroll general ledger reconciliation is the month-end procedure proving payroll in the ledger agrees to the register, the deposits, the bank, and the liabilities. The sync from Gusto, Rippling, or ADP creates the entry. It never tests it.


A sync is data movement.


A reconciliation is an assertion with evidence behind it, and indinero’s CPAs run it as a named step in every monthly close instead of a year-end cleanup.


The source document is the payroll register. ADP’s[definition of a payroll register](https://www.adp.com/resources/articles-and-insights/articles/w/what-is-a-payroll-register.aspx) lists pay dates, hours, rates, gross wages, employee and employer taxes, benefit deductions, net wages, and payment detail, and names reconciling payroll expense to the general ledger as a primary use. One report, four structurally different kinds of number:


- **Expense.** Gross wages, employer taxes, employer benefit contributions.
- **Employee-funded liability.** Withholding, employee FICA, 401(k) deferrals, benefit deductions, garnishments.
- **Employer-funded liability.** Employer FICA, FUTA, SUTA, employer match, unremitted benefit contributions.
- **Cash.** Net pay disbursed, plus the provider’s tax and fee debits.


A defensible payroll reconciliation month end cadence follows the filing calendar, not preference. Prove the clearing account every pay run, tie the ledger monthly, agree Form 941 quarterly, agree Forms W-2 and W-3 annually. The IRS[employment tax due dates](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/employment-tax-due-dates) page, updated April 21, 2026, puts the 941 deadlines at April 30, July 31, October 31, and January 31, with 10 additional days when every deposit was timely, and W-2 with W-3 at the SSA by January 31.


Then keep the workpaper, not just the result. IRS[employment tax recordkeeping guidance](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/employment-tax-recordkeeping) , reviewed June 12, 2026, calls for employment tax records to be held at least four years after the fourth-quarter filing. Four years outlasts most payroll vendor relationships. A controller who saved the tie-out answers an IRS notice in days. One who didn’t rebuilds it from a provider that may no longer be the incumbent, so file it with your other[book-closing](https://www.indinero.com/blog/business-bookkeeping-closing-your-companys-books/) evidence and scope it into your[online bookkeeping services](https://www.indinero.com/services/online-bookkeeping-services/) engagement.


## Why a Payroll Sync Is Not a Reconciliation


A payroll sync posts what you configured it to post. On a Gusto-fed ledger, that often means there’s no payroll tax liability balance to reconcile at all.


Gusto’s help center is explicit about why. Its[General Ledger Mapper documentation](https://support.gusto.com/article/221020155120720/map-payroll-data-and-download-reports-with-the-general-ledger-mapper) and[Xero integration article](https://support.gusto.com/article/103000325100000/integrate-with-xero) state that tax payments do not appear on your balance sheet as a liability, because Gusto handles taxes on a cash basis rather than accrual and treats each payroll’s tax debit as closed. Employer taxes sync as expense. The[QuickBooks Online integration](https://support.gusto.com/article/100971895100000/integrate-with-quickbooks-online) pushes a journal entry every pay run from the mapped chart of accounts.


Read the consequence carefully. Books built that way are right on a cash basis in the month the debit clears and wrong in any month where the pay date and the tax debit fall on opposite sides of the cutoff. That isn’t a mapping error. It’s a design choice the close has to answer with a manual accrual.


Justworks shows the same gap from another angle. Its[QuickBooks Online integration](https://help.justworks.com/hc/en-us/articles/10279095459355-QuickBooks-Online-Integration) and[accounting integrations](https://www.justworks.com/product-updates/accounting-integrations) transfer invoice data, posted as a Bill or a Journal Entry. In a PEO model the artifact reaching the ledger is a service invoice. Legitimate record of cash out. Not a decomposed register, and nothing in it separates wages from employer tax from withholding.


Rippling and ADP put the risk in the configuration instead. Rippling’s[payroll journal entry guidance](https://www.rippling.com/blog/payroll-journal-entry) describes a summarized per-run export mapped into GL dimensions by department, work location, and pay type, with exception rules. ADP’s[RUN General Ledger guide](https://support.adp.com/adp_payroll/content/hybrid/GL/RUN_GL_Guide_QBO.pdf) has the employer map payroll items against its own chart of accounts, exporting either one summary entry or one per employee. Payroll journal entry mapping that was right the day it was built goes quietly wrong the month after a reorg.


Not one of these syncs asserts the mapping is correct, that a liability equals what’s still owed, or that the expense landed in the right period. The IRS publishes its own[reconciling worksheet for Forms 941, W-2, and W-3](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-tege/year-end_reconciliation_worksheet.pdf) because the government doesn’t take the sync’s word for it either. Provider choice still matters, and[choosing a payroll provider for a growing SaaS company](https://www.indinero.com/blog/choosing-payroll-provider-for-growing-saas/) is a real decision. It just isn’t the same one as proving the close.


## The Balances That Have to Agree


Four agreements carry the procedure. Controllers who reconcile payroll to general ledger accounts monthly test all four and name the evidence behind each one.


Agreement What you prove Evidence Cadence


Gross wages Register gross for every pay date in the period equals wage expense, after the opening accrual reverses Register, accrual entries Monthly


Employer taxes Register employer tax equals employer tax expense and the deposit record. At quarter-end, the filed return too Register, EFTPS confirmations, provider tax debit, Form 941 Monthly to deposits, quarterly to the filing


Net pay Register net pay equals cash actually out the door Bank statement, deposit debit, checks presented, paycard loads Every pay run


Liability balances Each balance equals a named, dated obligation still owed Roll-forward schedule per account Monthly


One correction before you build the workpaper. “Employer taxes to the filings” isn’t a monthly test, because[Form 941](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i941) is quarterly. In months one and two of a quarter the only testable comparison is the register against the deposit record, which[IRS Publication 15](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) requires to be an electronic funds transfer with a retrievable confirmation. Write the monthly test and the quarterly test as separate lines, or the procedure stalls two months out of every three.


This is also the part a bank reconciliation never reaches.[Reconciling business bank accounts](https://www.indinero.com/blog/business-account-reconciliation/) proves cash. It says nothing about whether accrued wages, withheld tax, or employer FUTA are stated correctly, because none of those balances touch the statement in the month they arise.


### Gross Wages and Employer Taxes


Gross wages are the easiest test and the one most often passed by accident. It fails for three recurring reasons: a pay date recorded in the wrong month, an off-cycle or bonus run that never synced, and wage expense reclassified between departments after the sync posted.


Employer taxes are harder, because the expected amount has to be recomputed rather than accepted.


Item 2026 figure Employer share Source


Social Security 6.2% each side Matched[IRS Pub 15](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15)


Social Security wage base $184,500, up $8,400 from $176,100 Both sides[PayrollOrg, October 24, 2025](https://payroll.org/news-resources/news/news-detail/2025/10/24/social-security-wage-base-increases-to-$184-500-for-2026)


Maximum Social Security tax per side $11,439 Each[PayrollOrg](https://payroll.org/news-resources/news/news-detail/2025/10/24/social-security-wage-base-increases-to-$184-500-for-2026)


Medicare 1.45% each side, no wage cap Matched[IRS Topic 751](https://www.irs.gov/taxtopics/tc751) , updated September 24, 2026


Additional Medicare Tax 0.9% above $200,000 None. Employee only[Form 941 instructions, Rev. March 2026](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i941)


FUTA 6.0% on the first $7,000, 5.4% standard credit, 0.6% net Employer only[IRS FUTA credit reduction](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/futa-credit-reduction)


SUTA wage base State-specific, $7,000 to $78,200 Employer only in most states[2026 state SUI bases](https://payroll-solution.com/state-unemployment-insurance-taxable-wage-bases-for-2026-2/)


The 941 instructions say it plainly. “Additional Medicare Tax is only imposed on the employee. There is no employer share of Additional Medicare Tax.” Compute expected employer Medicare as 1.45% of Medicare wages plus 0.9% of the excess and you overstate employer tax every quarter.


FUTA carries a timing trap. California’s final 2025 credit reduction landed at[1.2%, the U.S. Virgin Islands at 4.5%](https://payroll.org/news-resources/news/news-detail/2025/11/11/california-virgin-islands-face-futa-credit-reduction-for-2025) . For 2026 both are still only[potential reductions](https://payroll.org/news-resources/news/news-detail/2026/04/07/california-and-virgin-islands-may-face-credit-reduction-for-2026) , California at 1.5% or as high as 5.3% if the 3.8% Benefit Cost Rate add-on isn’t waived by July 1, the Virgin Islands at 4.8%, and nothing is determined until after November 10, 2026. Accrue 0.6% all year and the real rate arrives in Q4 as an unbooked liability. The[mechanics of employer payroll tax](https://www.indinero.com/blog/define-payroll-tax/) repeat every month. The rate doesn’t.


### Withholding and Benefit Liability Accounts


Every withheld dollar is somebody else’s money parked in your account until you remit it, so each balance needs a roll-forward: beginning balance, accruals, remittances, named ending obligation.


- **Federal income tax and both sides of FICA.**[Pub 15](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) section 11 sets the lookback period as the four quarters ending June 30 of the prior year. At $50,000 or less you deposit monthly, by the 15th of the following month. Above $50,000, semiweekly.
- **State withholding and SUTA.** One balance per state, on that state’s own calendar, rate, and wage base. This is where a company that hired remotely finds the registration nobody finished, which ties this reconciliation to[multi-state payroll compliance](https://www.indinero.com/blog/multi-state-payroll-compliance-for-growing-saas/) .
- **401(k) deferrals, loan repayments, and match.** The[2026 limits](https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/401k-limit-increases-to-24500-for-2026-ira-limit-increases-to-7500) released November 13, 2025 are a $24,500 deferral, $8,000 age-50 catch-up, $11,250 for ages 60 through 63, and $72,000 in annual additions under[Notice 2025-67](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/n-25-67.pdf) . Accrue the match to the period the compensation relates to, not the quarter the wire clears.
- **Health, dental, vision, HSA, and FSA.** Deductions taken less premiums remitted. A chronic residual means the deduction schedule and the carrier invoice have drifted, which is a real expense or a real employee refund.
- **Garnishments and child support.** Held in trust, remitted on a court or agency calendar, never netted against anything.


The deferral deadline is the rule most often stated wrong. Under[29 CFR 2510.3-102(a)(1)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/2510.3-102) , contributions become plan assets “as of the earliest date on which such contributions or repayments can reasonably be segregated from the employer’s general assets.” Paragraph (b)(1) adds an outer limit of the 15th business day of the month following receipt. That’s a ceiling, not a safe harbor. The only safe harbor is the 7-business-day rule in (a)(2)(i), and it reaches only plans with fewer than 100 participants at the start of the plan year. A late deferral is a prohibited transaction on Schedule H Line 4a, per the DOL’s[delinquent contributions FAQ](https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/EBSA/about-ebsa/our-activities/resource-center/faqs/delinquent-participant-contributions-reporting.pdf) , corrected through the[Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/ebsa/employers-and-advisers/plan-administration-and-compliance/correction-programs/vfcp) , whose Self-Correction Component took effect March 17, 2025. Lost earnings get restored, and correction can’t be paid from plan assets.


## Where the Differences Come From


Differences cluster in seven places, and none of them show up on a bank statement.


1. **The payroll clearing account never returns to zero.** OnPay’s[guide to payroll clearing accounts](https://onpay.com/insights/payroll-clearing-accounts-explained/) , updated September 18, 2025, has the balance returning to zero once every distribution in the cycle completes. The qualifier is the cycle. A residual where the provider debit and the pay date straddle the cutoff is an in-transit item with a clearing date. The same residual three months running is a plug.
2. **The pay period straddles month-end.** Gross for the last full pay period, divided by days in the period, times days in the stub, posted on the final day and reversed on day one. Carry employer taxes on the accrued wages or employer FICA is short by roughly 7.65% of the stub. Two months a year get three pay dates.
3. **The sync posted a summary entry nobody proved.** A Gusto-fed ledger with no tax liability account, a Justworks-fed ledger holding an invoice, a Rippling mapping that predates the reorg, an ADP RUN export locked to single-entry mode.
4. **Employer and employee FICA are commingled.** They’re equal for Social Security and regular Medicare, which is exactly why they get netted. Then Form 941 breaks the symmetry. Lines 5a and 5b apply a combined 0.124 factor and line 5c applies 0.029, so the 941 FICA amounts run roughly double W-2 Boxes 4 and 6. Halve them before comparing, or correct books look broken.
5. **PTO policy doesn’t match the standard.** PwC’s[ASC 710 compensated absences guidance](https://viewpoint.pwc.com/dt/us/en/pwc/accounting_guides/pensions-and-employee-benefitspeb/peb_guide/Chapter-6-PEB/64_Compensated_absences_8.html) , published September 22, 2026, needs all four criteria met before an accrual exists, including that the right vest or accumulate, and ASC 710-10-25-7 doesn’t require accrual for nonvesting accumulating sick pay. Use-it-or-lose-it vacation in a state with no mandatory payout generally doesn’t accrue. Read the policy and the state law, don’t assume.
6. **An equity vest changes the deposit calendar.** Supplemental wages withhold at 22%, and 37% above $1,000,000 in a year. Accumulate $100,000 of employment taxes on any day and the deposit is due the next business day, and a monthly depositor who trips it becomes semiweekly for the rest of that year and the following one. PwC’s[share-based payment withholding guidance](https://viewpoint.pwc.com/dt/us/en/pwc/accounting_guides/stockbased_compensat/stockbased_compensat__3_US/chapter_3_liabilityc_US/33_criteria_for_dete_US/336_tax_withholding_US.html) adds the other half, since equity classification holds only while withholding stays inside maximum statutory rates by jurisdiction.[Equity compensation through payroll](https://www.indinero.com/blog/equity-compensation-payroll-for-saas/) is one event with two sets of consequences.
7. **Department or class mapping drifted.** Headcount is the largest line in a SaaS P&L, and mapping is what turns payroll into R&D, S&M, G&A, and COGS. Drift distorts gross margin, R&D credit qualified wages, and every per-department board metric, and the balance sheet still foots.


The stakes aren’t evenly spread. A stale balance in a withheld tax account is categorically worse than a stale employer tax balance, because withheld amounts are trust funds. IRS[Trust Fund Recovery Penalty](https://www.irs.gov/individuals/international-taxpayers/trust-fund-recovery-penalty) guidance, reviewed February 6, 2026, assesses the full unpaid trust fund tax plus interest personally against a responsible person, and says “you are acting willfully if you pay other expenses of the business instead of the withholding taxes.”


Those aren’t your dollars.


The mismatch also reports itself, slowly. Under[Combined Annual Wage Reporting](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/combined-annual-wage-reporting-employment-tax-problem-inquiries) , reviewed February 4, 2026, Forms 94X are matched against processed Forms W-2, case review begins in April for the second preceding tax year, and the employer gets 45 days to answer Letter 99C. A Q3 2026 failure surfaces in spring 2028. Understated accruals surface faster in a transaction, where bonus and PTO gaps become a working capital adjustment, which is why[due diligence](https://www.indinero.com/blog/due-diligence-what-why-how/) and[audit prep](https://www.indinero.com/blog/audit-prep-for-startups-checklist/) both start at the payroll liability roll-forward.


## CPA-Led vs Bookkeeper-Led


The difference isn’t care or competence. It’s which judgments the engagement is scoped and credentialed to make. A professional-standards line sits underneath it, since AICPA guidance on[AR-C Section 70](https://www.aicpa-cima.com/news/article/aicpa-to-clarify-applicability-of-standards-to-financial-statements-prepared) treats entering transactions and making journal entries as bookkeeping assistance, while preparing financial statements is a separate nonattest service with its own engagement requirements.


Recording payroll and asserting payroll is right are two different jobs.


Judgment in this procedure Bookkeeper-led typically CPA-led


The sync posted Confirms it ran and the bank cleared Ties gross, employer taxes, net pay, and every liability balance to the register and the deposit record


Cash-basis tax treatment in the sync Books follow the sync, so no tax liability appears Books the accrual the sync omits, so the period is right


ASC 710 PTO Repeats last year, or accrues nothing Tests written policy and state payout law against all four criteria, documents the conclusion


A $100,000 single-day accumulation Not monitored Flags the next-business-day deposit and the two-year cadence change before anything is late


401(k) remittance timing Sees the wire cleared Tests against the plan-asset rule, knows whether the 7-business-day safe harbor applies


Form 941 to W-3 tie-out Provider filed it, considered done Reconciles four returns to the register and the W-3, halves the combined factors, keeps the workpaper


A bookkeeper-led close answers whether the transactions got recorded. A CPA-led close answers whether the period is right under GAAP and provable to an auditor, a buyer, or the IRS three years later, which is why the IRS[year-end reconciliation worksheet](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-tege/year-end_reconciliation_worksheet.pdf) belongs in your file rather than a provider’s dashboard. Payroll is where those two answers separate fastest, because payroll is the largest expense, a trust-fund obligation, an ERISA obligation, and an accrual judgment at once. That’s why indinero staffs[accounting services](https://www.indinero.com/services/accounting-services/) with credentialed CPAs instead of treating the close as data entry.


## How Indinero Reconciles Payroll on Every Close


Indinero runs payroll to the ledger as a documented twelve-step procedure inside the monthly close, with a CPA owning the judgments rather than the sync status.


1. Pull the register for every pay date in the period, including off-cycle, bonus, and equity-vest runs.
2. Agree register gross to wage expense, after the opening accrual reverses and before the closing one posts.
3. Recompute employer taxes against the $184,500 Social Security base, uncapped Medicare, FUTA at the expected effective rate, and each state’s SUTA base, confirming no employer share landed on the 0.9%.
4. Agree net pay to the bank, separating the deposit debit, checks presented, paycard loads, the provider’s tax debit, and its fee debit.
5. Roll forward every liability account and tie each ending balance to a named, dated obligation.
6. Prove the payroll clearing account. Zero, or an in-transit item with a clearing date.
7. Book the stub-period accrual with employer taxes on the accrued wages, reversing on day one.
8. Test the PTO accrual against the current written policy and applicable state payout rules.
9. Test deferral remittance dates against[29 CFR 2510.3-102](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/2510.3-102) and the correct participant count.
10. Re-test department, class, and location mapping against the current org chart.
11. At quarter-end, reconcile the register to Form 941 with the combined factors in hand.
12. At year-end, reconcile the four returns to Form W-3 using the[IRS worksheet](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-tege/year-end_reconciliation_worksheet.pdf) , then save the file for the four-year window.


Three things make that repeatable. Accrual treatment is the default rather than an upgrade, which matters most where the provider’s sync is cash-basis by design. The work happens inside your own QuickBooks Online or Xero, so the mapping table, the clearing account, and the workpapers stay where your auditor and a buyer’s diligence team will look for them. And bookkeeping, accounting, tax, and fractional CFO advisory sit in one monthly engagement, pricing starts at $750/mo, so the person who reconciles the withheld-tax liability and the person who answers Letter 99C two years later are on the same team.


A sync tells you the entry posted. The reconciliation tells you the period is right.


## Frequently asked questions


Most questions about this procedure come down to one thing, which is how much the provider’s integration actually proves. Here are the answers Controllers and finance leads ask us for most.


### Doesn’t my payroll provider already post the entries correctly?


A payroll provider posts what you configured it to post, which is not the same as proving the entries are right. Gusto’s own documentation states that tax payments don’t appear on your balance sheet as a liability, because it handles taxes on a cash basis. Mapping that was right the day it was built goes quietly wrong the month after a reorg, and no sync asserts otherwise.


### How often should payroll be reconciled to the books?


Reconcile payroll to the ledger monthly, prove the clearing account every pay run, agree Form 941 quarterly, and agree Forms W-2 and W-3 annually. The cadence follows the filing calendar. Form 941 is due April 30, July 31, October 31, and January 31, and Forms W-2 and W-3 reach the SSA by January 31. In the first two months of a quarter the only testable comparison is the register against the deposit record.


### Why do payroll liabilities sit on the balance sheet forever?


Payroll liabilities go stale because nobody rolls them forward, so no balance is ever tied to a named, dated obligation still owed. A withheld tax balance that never clears is worse than a stale employer tax balance, because withheld amounts are trust funds. The IRS assesses the full unpaid trust fund tax plus interest personally against a responsible person. A chronic residual in a benefit account means the deduction schedule and the carrier invoice have drifted.


### How do I accrue wages when a pay period crosses month-end?


Prorate the last full pay period’s gross wages across the stub days, post that accrual on the final day, and reverse on day one. Carry employer taxes on the accrued wages too, or employer FICA runs short by roughly 7.65% of the stub. Two months a year get three pay dates, which is where a straight repeat of last month’s entry breaks. Indinero’s CPAs book that accrual as a named close step rather than a year-end cleanup.


### Should payroll post in summary or employee by employee?


Posting payroll as a summary entry is fine, provided department, class, and location mapping is correct and the register stays on file. ADP’s RUN export runs either way, one summary entry or one per employee, and Rippling maps a summarized per-run export into GL dimensions. Employee-level detail belongs in the register, which the IRS expects you to keep at least four years after the fourth-quarter filing. The mapping still has to be re-tested against the current org chart.


### What does this reconciliation prove during an audit?


Payroll general ledger reconciliation proves wage expense landed in the right period and that every liability balance equals a named, dated obligation still owed. Auditors and diligence teams both start at the payroll liability roll-forward, because understated bonus and PTO accruals become a working capital adjustment in a transaction. The workpaper is the evidence, so keep the roll-forward schedules, the register, the deposit confirmations, and the Form 941 tie-out in your own files.


### Is payroll reconciliation included in a standard bookkeeping engagement?


Payroll reconciliation sits outside most bookkeeping scopes, which record the entry and confirm the bank cleared rather than test the balances. AICPA guidance on AR-C Section 70 treats entering transactions and making journal entries as bookkeeping assistance, with preparing financial statements as a separate service. With indinero, the reconciliation is a named step in the monthly close, and bookkeeping, accounting, tax, and fractional CFO advisory sit in one engagement inside your own QuickBooks Online or Xero.
